meta.subtitle: Raised Fiscal 2027 guidance after a 14% first-quarter revenue gain; pricing power and net cash against discretionary-demand and tariff risk.

analystSentiment.commentary: Ralph Lauren enters Fiscal 2027 with momentum. In the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, the 13-week period ended June 27, 2026, revenue rose 14% to $2.0 billion on a reported basis and 13% in constant currency. Diluted EPS reached $4.28, up 22% versus the first quarter of Fiscal 2026, and adjusted EPS was $4.59. Management raised its full-year Fiscal 2027 outlook, now guiding constant-currency revenue growth centered around 5% to 6% and operating-margin expansion of approximately 60 to 80 basis points in constant currency. The shares trade at $337.47, below the 52-week high of $421.60 and well under the $446.71 consensus target. We rate the stock BUY with a $360 to $415 target range. The core support is a heritage brand with demonstrated pricing power, a net-cash balance sheet, and consistent capital return, set against the discretionary-demand and tariff risks the company itself flags.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Ralph Lauren Corporation designs, markets, and distributes luxury lifestyle products across apparel, handbags, footwear and accessories, fragrances, home, and hospitality. Founded in 1967 and based in New York, the company sells under brands including Ralph Lauren Collection, Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Double RL, Lauren Ralph Lauren, RLX Ralph Lauren, Polo Ralph Lauren Children, and Chaps. It reaches consumers through three channels, retail, wholesale, and licensing, and diversifies across North America, Europe, and Asia so results do not depend on any single region or channel. The direct-to-consumer channel spans retail stores, concession-based shop-within-shops, and digital commerce; wholesale runs principally through department stores, specialty stores, and third-party digital partners. In Fiscal 2026 the company generated $8.1 billion of revenue, up 14.6%, with a 69.9% gross margin and $941.1 million of net income, or $15.11 of diluted EPS.

thesis.label: BUY
thesis.body: The investment case rests on brand-driven pricing power translating into margin expansion. In the first quarter of Fiscal 2027 average unit retail rose across the direct-to-consumer network with lower-than-planned promotions, and gross and operating margins expanded, as the income commentary details. Growth was broad, with revenue advancing in all three reportable segments, led by Asia and North America. The balance sheet carries net cash, and management returned capital to shareholders in the quarter while raising its full-year outlook. The counter-case is that Ralph Lauren sells discretionary luxury goods whose demand falls in downturns, and that tariffs and a promotional retail environment could compress the margins the thesis depends on.

catalysts: Raised Fiscal 2027 guidance: management now expects constant-currency revenue growth centered around 5% to 6% and operating-margin expansion of approximately 60 to 80 basis points in constant currency, up from its prior outlook.
Asia acceleration: the region kept outpacing total-company growth in the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, led by strength in China, as the segment detail sets out.
Pricing power: average unit retail rose across the direct-to-consumer network with lower-than-planned promotions, supporting further gross-margin gains.
Capital return: the company repurchased approximately $250 million of Class A common stock in the quarter and keeps returning capital from a net-cash balance sheet.
Category breadth: high-potential categories, Women's Apparel, Outerwear, and Handbags, grew more than 20% in constant currency and outpaced total-company growth.
risks: Discretionary demand: luxury and discretionary purchases decline during economic weakness, high inflation, or rising rates, per the company's own risk factors.

Tariffs and trade policy: new U.S. tariffs and the uncertain status of IEEPA-related refunds pressure product costs; AUR growth and favorable mix more than offset that pressure this quarter, but the offset may thin as tariff rates rise later in the year.
Promotional environment: a prolonged promotional stance could compress the gross margin the thesis relies on, per management.
Founder and key-person concentration: the loss of Mr. Ralph Lauren or other senior leaders is a named risk, and his Class B holding concentrates voting control.
Currency: management expects foreign exchange to be a modest headwind to Fiscal 2027 revenue growth.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended 52-53 week year ending near March 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Revenue rose from $6.2 billion in Fiscal 2022 to $8.1 billion in Fiscal 2026, with growth accelerating to 14.6% in the latest fiscal year from 6.7% the year before. Gross margin has climbed to 69.9% in Fiscal 2026 from 66.7% in Fiscal 2022, operating margin reached 14.5%, and diluted EPS grew to $15.11 from $8.07 over the same span. The first quarter of Fiscal 2027, the 13-week period ended June 27, 2026, extended the trend: revenue increased 14% to $2.0 billion reported and 13% in constant currency, with foreign currency adding about 60 basis points. Gross margin in the quarter was 73.7%, up 140 basis points, driven by the 15% AUR gain and favorable channel and geographic mix that more than offset tariff and product-cost pressure. Reported operating income was $342 million at a 17.5% margin; on an adjusted basis operating income was $366 million at an 18.7% margin, 170 basis points above the prior year. Net income was $262 million, or $4.28 per diluted share, versus $220 million and $3.52 a year earlier. The effective tax rate rose to about 23% from about 21%, reflecting the absence of favorable discrete tax benefits in the prior-year quarter.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended 52-53 week year ending near March 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: Ralph Lauren runs a net-cash balance sheet. At the end of Fiscal 2026 net debt was -$749.1 million, as cash and short-term investments of $2.1 billion exceeded total debt of $1.2 billion. Net debt to EBITDA was -0.3x on a trailing basis, and interest coverage was 22.4x. Total equity stood at $2.8 billion and the current ratio was 2.13 at fiscal year-end, or 2.04 on a trailing-twelve-month basis. The first quarter of Fiscal 2027 ended with $1.9 billion in cash and short-term investments and total debt little changed from year-end, both down from $2.3 billion of cash and $1.6 billion of debt a year earlier. Inventory fell 5% from the prior-year quarter, which management frames as well-positioned to demand. The balance sheet gives the company room to keep investing and returning capital through a downturn.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended 52-53 week year ending near March 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow was $1.2 billion in each of Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026, up from $0.7 billion in Fiscal 2022. Free cash flow reached $1.0 billion in Fiscal 2025 at a 14.4% margin; the Fiscal 2026 capital-expenditure and free-cash-flow lines were not captured in the pack. Cash generation comfortably covers reinvestment and shareholder returns. Management guides to Fiscal 2027 capital expenditure of approximately 4% to 5% of revenue. The dividend yields 1.16% at the current price, a secondary component of a total-return case led by buybacks.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: Ralph Lauren trades at $337.47, a 21.3x trailing P/E and 13.2x trailing EV/EBITDA. On forward estimates the multiple compresses: consensus Fiscal 2027 EPS is $18.90 and Fiscal 2028 EPS is $20.91, putting the shares at about 17.9x next-twelve-month earnings. Price-to-sales is 2.4x. The current price sits below the 52-week high of $421.60 and well under the $446.71 consensus target, which implies 32.4% upside; the street is 17 Buy, 1 Hold, and 1 Sell across 19 analysts, with a target range of $250.00 to $520.00 and a $455.00 median. No peer multiples were provided in the pack, so we anchor on the company's own forward multiples and history rather than a cross-sectional comparison. At roughly 16.1x Fiscal 2028 earnings, the shares are not demanding for a brand compounding revenue in the mid-single digits with expanding margins.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Asia and the high-potential categories sustain double-digit growth, AUR gains hold, and margins expand at the upper end of guidance, driving a re-rating toward the high end of the street's target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue grows in line with the raised Fiscal 2027 outlook of mid-single digits in constant currency, operating margin expands 60 to 80 basis points, and the multiple holds near current forward levels.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: A discretionary-spending slowdown and a more promotional environment stall revenue and compress gross margin, and the multiple derates as luxury demand weakens.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: We weight the Base case at 45%, the Bull case at 30%, and the Bear case at 25%. The probability-weighted fair value sits above the current price of $337.47, which is what supports the BUY rating and the $360 to $415 target range. The Bear case is a genuine scenario, not a formality: it places the stock roughly 18% below the current price, consistent with the company's warning that luxury demand contracts in downturns and that a prolonged promotional stance would pressure gross margin. The Bull case leans on the Asia trajectory set out in the segment detail, and on AUR-led margin expansion. The main swing factor between Base and Bear is whether the raised guidance survives a weaker consumer and higher tariff costs in the back half of the year.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The vendor tearsheet does not break out a revenue mix and shows only the consolidated total, but the earnings press release reports North America, Europe, and Asia as the Company's three reportable segments; we use the filing's segment detail. In the first quarter of Fiscal 2027 North America revenue grew 13% to $740 million, with segment operating income of $171 million at a 23.1% margin. Europe revenue rose 7% to $594 million on a reported basis and 5% in constant currency, delivering $157 million of operating income at a 26.4% margin. Asia revenue rose 24% reported to $589 million and 25% in constant currency, producing $198 million of operating income at a 33.5% margin, and China grew more than 40%. Across the business, direct-to-consumer comparable store sales rose low-double-digits and wholesale accelerated to mid-teens growth.

moatFactors.name: Brand and pricing power
moatFactors.body: Ralph Lauren raises price while holding volume, direct evidence of brand-based pricing power. Average unit retail climbed across the direct-to-consumer network with lower-than-planned promotions in the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, and the resulting gross-margin expansion, detailed in the income commentary, extended a multi-year rise from a 69.9% full-year gross margin in Fiscal 2026.

moatFactors.name: Scale and diversification
moatFactors.body: The company balances three geographies, North America, Europe, and Asia, and three channels, retail, wholesale, and licensing, so results do not hinge on any single region or channel. Revenue reached $8.1 billion in Fiscal 2026.

moatFactors.name: Brand heritage and portfolio
moatFactors.body: Founded in 1967, Ralph Lauren markets a family of brands including Ralph Lauren Collection, Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Double RL, and Lauren Ralph Lauren across apparel, accessories, fragrances, home, and hospitality. The company continues to recruit new direct-to-consumer consumers and has over 70 million social media followers.

moatFactors.name: Financial resilience
moatFactors.body: A net-cash balance sheet, with $1.9 billion in cash and short-term investments against $1.2 billion of debt at the end of the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, and interest coverage of 22.4x, lets the brand invest and return capital through cycles.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is narrow rather than wide because Ralph Lauren competes in fashion and discretionary luxury, where consumer tastes shift and demand is cyclical. The brand's pricing power is real, shown by rising average unit retail with lower promotions and expanding gross margin, but it must be re-earned each season through product and marketing. The company's own risk factors acknowledge that luxury demand declines in downturns and that a prolonged promotional response would erode gross margin. Offsetting that, the balance sheet is strong and the brand's heritage, built over nearly 60 years, supports durability that a newer label would lack. On balance, the intangible brand asset is durable enough to defend above-average margins across a cycle, but not so entrenched as to be immune to fashion risk.

points: Revenue grew 14% to $2.0 billion in the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, and management raised its full-year outlook to constant-currency growth centered around 5% to 6%.
Asia is the growth engine: it led the company's three reportable segments in the quarter, and China's growth outpaced the rest of the region, as the segment detail sets out.
Beyond the flagship assortment, the Core business grew mid-teens and the high-potential categories outpaced the total company, broadening the growth base.
The direct-to-consumer network added 1.5 million new consumers in the quarter, supported by the average-unit-retail gains discussed in the financials.
The company opened 22 new owned and partnered stores in the quarter, expanding its key-city ecosystems.
Consensus sees revenue reaching $8.7 billion in Fiscal 2027 and $9.1 billion in Fiscal 2028.

management.leadership: Ralph Lauren serves as Executive Chairman and Chief Creative Officer, and Patrice Louvet is President and Chief Executive Officer. Management is executing the second year of its Next Great Chapter Drive plan, and the first quarter of Fiscal 2027 beat the company's own expectations across geographies and channels, prompting a raised full-year outlook. The stated priorities are recruiting new and younger consumers, strengthening core and high-potential categories, and developing key-city ecosystems in every region. The company's risk factors flag the loss of Mr. Ralph Lauren or other senior leaders as a specific risk, underscoring the founder's central role.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation favors reinvestment plus steady shareholder return from a position of balance-sheet strength. In Fiscal 2026 the company repurchased $623.8 million of stock and paid $216.5 million in dividends. In the first quarter of Fiscal 2027 it repurchased approximately $250 million of Class A common stock and returned more than $300 million to shareholders in total. Buybacks do the heavier lifting in the total-return case, while the balance sheet stays in a net cash position of -$749.1 million as of the end of Fiscal 2026. That funding cushion lets the company sustain returns without adding leverage.
management.governance: Governance rests on the proxy statement in the pack. The board is majority independent: all nine non-management director nominees, Angela Ahrendts, Frank A. Bennack, Jr., Cesar Conde, Debra Cupp, Linda Findley, Michael A. George, Valerie Jarrett, Darren Walker, and Wei Zhang, were determined to be independent, and every member of the Audit, Talent, Nominating, and Finance Committees is independent. In Fiscal 2026 the board met six times and each director attended at least 75% of the meetings of the board and committees on which they served. The key governance feature for investors is the dual-class structure: Mr. Ralph Lauren holds all of the Class B common stock and controls 85.5% of total voting power, so public Class A holders have limited say over control decisions. A Lead Independent Director presides over regular executive sessions of the independent directors.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider ownership is dominated by the founder. Mr. Ralph Lauren beneficially owns 21,881,276 shares of Class B common stock, 100% of that class, plus 73,107 Class A shares, for 85.5% of total voting power. All directors and executive officers as a group hold 259,050 Class A shares and that same block of Class B stock. Among institutions, BlackRock, Inc. holds 6.3% of the Class A, Vanguard Capital Management LLC 6.1%, and Vanguard Portfolio Management LLC 5.2%. Patrice Louvet holds 57,567 Class A shares. The concentration aligns the founder with long-term value but limits minority-holder influence.

idiosyncratic: Founder and key-person concentration: the risk factors name the loss of Mr. Ralph Lauren or other senior leaders as a specific risk, and his control of 85.5% of voting power through Class B stock concentrates both creative and governance authority in one person.

Tariffs and trade policy: the company cites new U.S. tariffs following the Supreme Court's invalidation of the IEEPA tariffs, uncertain refund status for previously collected IEEPA duties, and possible retaliatory measures as pressures on product costs. AUR growth and favorable channel and geographic mix more than offset that incremental pressure in the first quarter of Fiscal 2027, with gross margin still expanding 140 basis points. Management expects a lower prevailing tariff rate only through the first half of the fiscal year, so the offset may not persist as rates rise in the back half.

Promotional and inventory risk: management warns that gross margins could be hurt if it applies a promotional strategy over a prolonged period, and that misjudging demand could leave it with excess or short inventory.

Wholesale timing and customer concentration: North America wholesale growth of 22% included about 15 points from resumed shipments to a single luxury wholesale account and timing shifts, so part of the quarter's strength may not repeat, and the financial difficulties of large wholesale customers are a named risk.
Currency translation: revenue and margins are exposed to foreign-exchange swings, and management expects currency to reduce Fiscal 2027 revenue growth by approximately 50 to 100 basis points.
risks.systemic: The systemic risks are those of a discretionary-luxury seller in an uncertain macro environment. The company's risk factors state that consumer purchases of discretionary and luxury items decline during economic weakness, high inflation, or rising interest rates. They also cite ongoing military conflicts, including those involving Iran and other hostilities in the Middle East, and the resulting pressure on consumer sentiment, energy prices, and currencies. A prolonged promotional environment across U.S. and European retail could force the company to discount and compress gross margin. Roughly a quarter of the value in our scenario set reflects these economy-wide risks materializing at once, which is why the Bear case is weighted at 25%.

body: We rate Ralph Lauren BUY with a target range of $360 to $415. The first quarter of Fiscal 2027 showed 14% reported revenue growth, a 73.7% gross margin up 140 basis points, and $4.28 of diluted EPS up 22%, and management raised full-year guidance. The stock trades at $337.47, a 21.3x trailing P/E and about 16.1x Fiscal 2028 earnings, below its 52-week high of $421.60 and well under the $446.71 consensus target.

The case combines a heritage brand with proven pricing power, a net-cash balance sheet, and steady capital return, set against genuine discretionary-demand, tariff, and promotional risks. Our probability-weighted fair value sits above the current price, and the reward outweighs the bear-case downside, but not by enough to justify a more aggressive call than BUY. We would grow more constructive if Asia momentum and AUR gains hold through a season of weaker consumer spending, and more cautious if guidance is cut.
